tool.name: sincei scCountReads features
tool.description: count reads per cell over BED/GTF features

param.label: BED/GTF files
param.help: BED/GTF files to limit the coverage analysis to the regions in them, e.g. genes for scRNA-seq or peaks for scATAC-seq.

param.label: Metagene
param.help: When either a BED12 or GTF file is used to provide regions, perform the computation on the merged exons, rather than using the genomic interval defined by the 5-prime and 3-prime most transcript bound (i.e., columns 2 and 3 of a BED file). If a BED3 or BED6 file is used as input, then columns 2 and 3 are used as an exon.

param.label: Transcript ID
param.help: When a GTF file is used to provide regions, only entries with this value as their feature (column 3) will be processed as transcripts.

validator.message: Only alphanumeric characters and underscores are allowed

param.label: Exon ID
param.help: When a GTF file is used to provide regions, only entries with this value as their feature (column 3) will be processed as exons. CDS would be another common value for this.

validator.message: Only alphanumeric characters and underscores are allowed

param.label: Transcript ID designator
param.help: Each region has an ID (e.g., ACTB) assigned to it, which for BED files is either column 4 (if it exists) or the interval bounds. For GTF files this is instead stored in the last column as a key:value pair (e.g., as 'transcript_id ACTB', for a key of transcript_id and a value of ACTB). In some cases it can be convenient to use a different identifier, e.g. gene_name. To do so, set this to the desired key.

validator.message: Only alphanumeric characters and underscores are allowed

tool.help:
**What it does**
`scCountReads features` counts, for each cell barcode in the whitelist, the reads overlapping each region of one or more BED or GTF files. A common use is counting scRNA-seq reads on genes, or scATAC/scChIP reads on peaks. The result is a cells x features count matrix.
Use **scCountReads bins** to count over fixed-size genomic bins instead.
-----
**Inputs**
- One or more BED/GTF files with the features. - One or more BAM files with a cell barcode tag. The dataset name (without `.bam`) is used as the sample label, so cells are named `label::barcode`. - A barcode whitelist.
**Outputs**
- An AnnData (`h5ad`) object with cells as observations and features as variables. @HELP_FOOTER@
